newsitem.title: UK: UK's Threadneedle plans major retail fund drive.
newsitem.headline: UK's Threadneedle plans major retail fund drive.

text.p: Threadneedle Asset Management said on Wednesday it planned a major offensive in the UK retail market and aimed to significantly grow market share in coming years.
It said it had applied to the Securities and Investments Board for authorisation of a multi-compartment open-ended investment company (OEIC), constituted as an umbrella fund.
It will provide a range of 23 funds covering all major stock markets, and it expects to be the largest OEIC in the UK.

It said the 26 unit trusts of Allied Dunbar and 12 of Eagle Star would be converted to form the basis of the new OEIC over the coming months once a review of the combined fund range has been undertaken.
Threadneedle, Allied Dunbar and Eagle Star are all owned by B.A.T. Industries. The new Threadneedle retail business will trade under the name Threadneedle Investments.
The combined operation will make it the eighth largest unit trust manager in the UK, with 4.7 billion sterling under management
"We are already a big player and have the resources to match our ambitions to grow our share of the UK retail investment market," said Paul Manduca, chief executive of Threadneedle Investments.
"We will be competing head on with other retail investment houses like Perpetual, M&G, etc.," said Manduca.

OEICs are closely modelled on UK unit trusts, but have some critical differences. They will offer a single mid-market price rather than a bid-offer spread, and a corporate structure will allow them to borrow.
Manduca said there would be initial costs involved in launching the brand.

"If you are going to build a brand in the market place, you are going to spend some money inevitably," he said, without giving any figures. "Of course it is nothing like the cost buying a brand," he said.
The new business would not be in place for picking up business from building society windfalls as the new product will not be up and running before the end of August.
Manduca said the group would look to build a presence in the U.S. in time, but said there were no immediate plans for an acquisition.
"That is something that may or may not happen in the medium term...Investment houses tend to have something in the U.S. because it is the biggest market in the world."
Threadneedle Asset Management has over 32 billion sterling under management.
